newsitem.title: FRANCE: Framatome says in no hurry to find ally.
newsitem.headline: Framatome says in no hurry to find ally.

text.p: French state-controlled nuclear engineering group Framatome said on Tuesday that it was not in a hurry to strike an alliance after merger talks with GEC Alsthom ended unsuccesfully.
"We are profitable, financially sound, we have a good order book and enough work for our staff," a Framatome spokeswoman said.
"But in the longer run we believe that it would be good to have an industrial partner to boost our position on the market," she added.
Framatome is battling for export orders with ABB Asea Brown Boveri and Westinghouse Electric Corp of the U.S.
While former Framatome chairman Jean-Claude Leny was vehemently opposed to any merger or deal, current head Dominique Vignon is open to discussions.
The name of a partner does not need to be GEC Alsthom or Germany's Siemens AG with which it has the Nuclear Power International joint-venture and is developing a new nuclear reactor.
But whatever will happen, France wants to keep a majority.

"The nuclear engineering know-how is very important for France -- some 75 percent of electricity is generated by nuclear powerstations -- and it is very logical that we want to keep control," an industry ministry source said.
"At the same time we are not blind to international developments and are open for alliances," he added.

The next step in the Framatome situation is up to Alcatel Alsthom, which has a 44 percent stake in Framatome. The rest is owned by state groups CEA Industrie, Electricite de France and the Consortium de Realisation (CDR).
For many years, Alcatel's former chairman Pierre Suard had been trying unsuccessfully to get government permission to raise the company's stake beyond 50 percent.

New chairman Serge Tchuruk, who arrived in 1995, made clear that he wanted to end the situation in which his group had 44 percent in Framatome and 50 percent in GEC Alsthom because this made it difficult to run effectively.

He planned a merger of Framatome in GEC Alsthom, with General Electric Co Plc seeing its stake diminish, and later wanted to float part of GEC Alsthom on the stock market to better focus the management.
But new GEC Plc managing director George Simpson, who succeeded Lord Weinstock last year, did not want to see his company's stake in GEC Alsthom diminish.

"Tchuruk has said in the past that the stakes in Framatome and GEC Alsthom were unmanageable, that we needed to increase our stakes or reduce them. It is not on the agenda but hypothetically we could cut our stake," an Alcatel source said.

In March, Tchuruk said that the company was conducting talks with GEC about their relationship in GEC Alsthom. The companies are also talking about defence electronics with GEC wanting to join in a bid for the state's 58 percent in Thomson-CSF -- either the one by Alcatel or a rival bid by Lagardere Groupe.
